title: 2026 specified-generator permit and ELV QA controls

sources.title: Specified generator: comply with permit conditions

facts.source_fact: Specified-generator permits are standalone permits covering SO2, NOx and dust emissions to air, not water, land, energy efficiency, odour or noise.
facts.expected_handling: Keep the permit scope limited to its stated air-emission categories.

facts.source_fact: The guidance distinguishes standard-rules, simple-bespoke and complex-bespoke specified-generator permits.
facts.expected_handling: Tag each application with the correct permit type.

facts.source_fact: A site permit may cover an individual specified generator or two or more generators operated for the same purpose.
facts.expected_handling: Preserve whether the permit object is a single generator or an aggregated site.

facts.source_fact: In England a standard-rules permit can only be used where the operator can meet the permit rules; otherwise a bespoke permit is required.
facts.expected_handling: Do not force an ineligible plant into a standard-rules pathway.

facts.source_fact: Natural Resources Wales no longer issues standard-rules permits for specified generators and uses bespoke permits.
facts.expected_handling: Apply jurisdiction-specific permit routing.

facts.source_fact: The stated standard-rules permits are available for low-risk Tranche B sites and not a mixture of Tranche A and B generators.
facts.expected_handling: Check tranche composition before selecting standard rules.

facts.source_fact: Standard rules are not suitable where the specified generator is also an MCP directly associated with an IED installation environmental permit.
facts.expected_handling: Route directly-associated IED plant away from this standard-rules route.

facts.source_fact: Applications require operator identity and declarations about relevant offences and bankruptcy or insolvency proceedings.
facts.expected_handling: Treat operator fitness declarations as required application data.

facts.source_fact: Applications require site location information and the NACE code for the activity.
facts.expected_handling: Preserve site and economic-activity classification provenance.

facts.source_fact: Generator location must be supplied as a national grid reference or latitude and longitude.
facts.expected_handling: Keep the supplied generator coordinates distinct from parcel geometry.

facts.source_fact: Net rated thermal input in MWth is required for the generator.
facts.expected_handling: Do not infer thermal input from electrical output.

facts.source_fact: The application requires generator type, such as engine or turbine.
facts.expected_handling: Carry plant technology type into permit screening.

facts.source_fact: The type and portion of fuels used must be reported using the relevant MCPD fuel categories.
facts.expected_handling: Preserve both fuel category and share.

facts.source_fact: Stack height is required application information.
facts.expected_handling: Do not substitute building height for stack height.

facts.source_fact: Expected annual operating hours and average load in use are required.
facts.expected_handling: Carry both annual hours and load assumptions into screening.

facts.source_fact: Applications require whether the plant is in an AQMA and its distance from human receptors.
facts.expected_handling: Keep air-quality-area and receptor-distance fields explicit.

facts.source_fact: Applicants must confirm a management system and declare its type and compliance with permit-management guidance.
facts.expected_handling: Treat management-system status as a permit application control.

facts.source_fact: Applicants must declare they can monitor each individual generator under the specified monitoring requirements and meet the ELVs.
facts.expected_handling: Do not treat site-level monitoring as proof for every individual generator unless the permit allows it.

facts.source_fact: Applications ask whether in-scope generators are being installed or substantially refurbished, or whether decarbonisation-readiness requirements are being applied voluntarily to existing plant.
facts.expected_handling: Gate CCR or HCR obligations on the stated readiness trigger.

facts.source_fact: Simple bespoke permits are low risk and do not require detailed air-dispersion modelling; complex bespoke permits are high risk and do require it.
facts.expected_handling: Do not omit detailed modelling for a complex bespoke case.

guard_patterns.handling: Preserve the cited source fact without broadening its scope.
Attach jurisdiction, permit type, plant/tranche status and pollutant scope.
Attach the guidance update date and current permit route.
Carry source URL, regulator and screening or monitoring provenance.
Do not convert generator permit information into parcel-level measured emissions without a separate binding gate.
